text:
kai: Quick heads-up — noticed a hit-rate drop in prefix cache when continuous batching is enabled on canary. p95 latency stayed similar but token cost jumped. Anyone else see this?

maria: 👀 saw a blip in the metrics dashboard earlier. Which workload? prod-sim or internal loadtest?

kai: prod-sim primarily. Batching window = 10ms, dynamic composition enabled. Hit rate on KV cache fell from ~72% -> ~48% for the assistant model.

anita: That's sizable. Do you have logs for cache keys being different? Could be key normalization change.

kai: Adding a quick trace:
```
cache.lookup(key="pfx:v1:user:123:hash( prompt[:128] )") -> MISS
cache.lookup(key="pfx:v1:anon:hash( prompt[:128] )") -> MISS
cache.lookup(key="pfx:v1:user:123:hash( prompt[:64] )") -> HIT
```
Seems like mixed key lengths and user-id variants.

sanjay: Hmm. Continuous batching mixes short and long prompts into same batch which triggers our adaptive keying fallback (we truncate to 64 when under memory budget). If some requests used 128 truncation and others 64 we end up with mismatched keys.

maria: So batch composition -> different truncation path -> cache fragmentation. Makes sense. What changed recently?

perf-bot: deploy-bot detected a kernel selection update on 1791236000 (PR #1142) that touched sequence-length heuristics.

kai: PR #1142 adjusted the kernel selection thresholds to favor tiled-attention kernels for sequences > 96. That also nudged the runtime to classify some requests as "long" earlier. Could be related.

anita: If classification changed, the prefix preprocessing might apply different normalization (we had a legacy rule: long sequences get normalized by token-windowing which affects prefix signature).

sanjay: Proposed quick repro: run the production trace driver with continuous-batcher on vs off, capture cache keys and batch composition stats. I ran one already:
- Continuous ON: avg batch size 6.2, mix_ratio (short:long) = 0.68, KV hit-rate = 47.9%, p50 = 38ms, p95 = 164ms, tokens/s = 120k
- Continuous OFF: avg batch size 2.1, mix_ratio = 0.92, KV hit-rate = 71.8%, p50 = 34ms, p95 = 158ms, tokens/s = 96k

kai: So continuous batching improves throughput but reduces cache effectiveness leading to higher token/sec (more tokens processed) and higher cost. Latency impact small but cost impact is real.

maria: We need a mitigation that preserves batching benefits without killing cache hit-rate. Ideas?

anita: 1) Make cache keying independent of transient kernel decisions — derive prefix signature purely from canonicalized token content, not sequence classifier. 2) Introduce batch-aware key canonicalization: normalize to a common truncation (e.g., 64) across requests before lookup, then if a longer prefix is needed, do a secondary fetch. 3) Warmup prefetch for top-K prefixes per batch composition.

sanjay: I prototyped option 2 in a branch: unify_truncation_for_cache. Results on the same replay: KV hit-rate -> 65.1%, avg batch size unchanged, p50 36ms, p95 162ms, token/sec 115k. Cost improved vs baseline continuous.

kai: Nice. Any edgecases? What about privacy/tenant isolation? We had user-specific keying too.

anita: We must keep tenant-id in the key. The issue was inconsistent inclusion of "user" vs "anon" in the runtime path when request metadata was lazily attached during batching. Fix: attach metadata at enqueue time.

maria: Also worried about warmup latencies when a long prefix is actually required and we only looked up a truncated key. Secondary fetch could add ~8-12ms.

sanjay: Measured secondary fetch latency: median 9ms, p95 28ms when cold. But most secondary fetches hit the backend quickly because we preloaded recent long keys in the cache.

kai: What's the rollout plan? We want to avoid regressions.

anita: Steps:
1) Patch: canonicalize cache keys (remove kernel/seq-class flags) + ensure tenant id set at enqueue.
2) Add batch-level canonical truncation (configurable per model).
3) Warmup: when batch contains >N requests with same prefix token-hash prefix, prefetch expanded KV entries.
4) Canary deploy to canary cluster for 48h with trace sampling.

maria: Can we add a guard to kernel selection so it doesn't flip classification mid-batch? That could minimize path divergence.

sanjay: Good call — add sticky classification per request at enqueue. If kernel selection changes later, we fallback to queued decision for that request. Avoids normalization divergence.

perf-bot: job perf/regression-checker started for 1791237890-canary-run.

kai: Also found a subtle perf regression in the cache LRU eviction code when batch mix is high: we saw more churn in the LRU pointers due to many tiny keys differing by truncation. After canonicalization churn drops ~40%.

anita: We should add a synthetic microbenchmark to the perf suite: generate interleaved batches with controlled short/long mix and measure cache hit-rate + LRU churn. Add to CI.

maria: Agreed. Also add alerts when KV hit-rate delta > 10% in 1h window post-deploy.

sanjay: One more thought — adaptive batching could try to co-locate similar prefixes in same micro-batch by hashing prefix-signature modulo #microbuckets. That keeps batch sizes but increases intra-batch homogeneity. Downside: potentially increases queueing for rare prefixes.

kai: We can simulate cost tradeoffs. sanjay — can you add a sim patch that implements microbucket co-location? If it shows >5% cost improvement without adding >15ms median queueing, ship to canary.

sanjay: On it. Quick numbers from a local sim: co-location -> KV hit-rate 73.2%, avg queue wait +3.4ms, token/sec -2%. Looks promising.

anita: Cool. Let's prioritize: canonical keying + enqueue metadata + LRU fix -> small canary. Microbucket co-location as next experiment. Warmup prefetch optional.

maria: I'll open the rollout RFC so eng/runtime + infra can sign off. Include the perf numbers and the mitigation timeline.

kai: Thanks all. We'll monitor perf/regression-checker and revert-if-needed rule set. :thumbsup:

deploy-bot: Canary rollout initiated: cluster canary-a, config=canonical-keying-v1, traffic=5% (1791238200)

perf-bot: Canary perf snapshot (1h): KV hit-rate delta vs baseline = +12.3%, p95 latency delta = +1.6ms, cost-estimated token spend delta = -7.8% (improvement).

maria: Early signals look good. Closing for now, will update RFC with final numbers tomorrow.

kai: Leaving traces/graphs in #eng-devex for follow-ups. Thanks.
